litigation_timing.support: All searches run 2026-10-22. (1) The law's subject: KNS_Bill row 162357 (ס"ח 1630, p. 186, published 1997-07-17); first-reading name 'חוק יסוד: הכנסת (תיקון מס. 34)' (1997-02-12), with no subtitle. The Nevo margin markers place '(תיקון מס' 24) תשנ"ז-1997' three times on s. 20 and once on s. 20A. A WebSearch (extended) for 1997 הכנסת אישרה תיקון לחוק יסוד הכנסת השעיה והעברה מכהונה של יושב ראש הכנסת או סגן יושב ראש returned the search tool's own summary that Amendment 24 added s. 20(c) (suspension), s. 20(d) (removal) and the acting-Speaker rule in s. 20A. The current text also has s. 20(b): restrictions on eligibility for Speaker or deputy, to be set in the Rules. So the subject is the Knesset's power to restrict, suspend and remove the Speaker and deputy Speakers. (2) Pending litigation: a WebSearch (extended) for בג"ץ עתירה נגד סגן יושב ראש הכנסת 1996 1997 כתב אישום העברה מתפקיד סגן יו"ר הכנסת found no petition. A WebSearch (extended) for רפאל פנחסי יו"ר ועדת הכנסת הורשע 1997 עתירה לבג"ץ להעבירו מתפקידו נדחתה found HCJ 7367/97, a petition against Pinhasi's election as chair of the House Committee. It followed his December 1997 conviction, so it was filed after this law passed (1997-07-09), and it concerned a committee chair, not the Speaker or a deputy. No Supreme Court case about the Speaker's or deputies' tenure was found pending on 1997-07-09.
litigation_timing.note: The law did not respond to any judgment that was found. The gazette text (fs.knesset.gov.il/14/law/14_lsr_211435.pdf) could not be read because the site is geo-blocked and the Wayback copy was refused, so the subject rests on the bill name, the Nevo markers and a search-tool summary.

A WebSearch (extended) for כינוס הכנסת בפגרה דרישת 25 חברי כנסת יושב ראש הכנסת סירב עתירה בג"ץ 1999 סעיף 33 חוק יסוד הכנסת found no petition from 1999-2000; the only petition it found was HCJ 706/19, which is later. litigation_timing.source: Versa English translation of HCJ 5167/00 Weiss v. Prime Minister, joined with HCJ 9607/00, 84/01, 86/01 and 147/01, decided 2001-01-25 (versa.cardozo.yu.edu/node/397); Knesset database mirror, BillID 169688; Hebrew Wikipedia 'חוק יסוד: ירושלים בירת ישראל'.
litigation_timing.support: Searches run 2026-10-22. The law (KNS_Bill 169688, ס"ח 1760, p. 28; names 'הצעת חוק-יסוד- ירושלים בירת ישראל (תיקון) (שטח השיפוט ופעילות שלטונית)') added s. 5 (Jerusalem's area is that set on 28 June 1967), s. 6 (no power relating to Jerusalem may be transferred to a foreign political or governmental body) and s. 7 (ss. 5-6 may be changed only by a Basic Law passed by a majority of MKs). A WebSearch (standard) for Weiss v. Prime Minister HCJ 5167/00 transitional government negotiations Jerusalem petition filed decided, and the Versa page itself, show the following. Weiss and Feiglin petitioned to stop the government's negotiations with the Palestinian Authority. The judgment lists 'Basic Law: Jerusalem, the Capital of Israel (Amendment)' among the Basic Laws cited. Para. 1 records that it and the 1999 Arrangements Law, 'which require ... Knesset decisions for any territorial changes, were mentioned', and that because the outgoing government had no Knesset majority 'even this narrows the authority of the outgoing government'. Para. 2 gives the Attorney General's position that any transfer of powers in Jerusalem to a foreign entity 'requires a basic law which is to be passed by a majority vote'. HCJ docket numbers are assigned in filing order, and number 5167 of 2000 points to a filing in about July 2000 (by comparison, 9607/00 was filed in December 2000 and 84/01 in January 2001). On that reading the petition was pending on 2000-11-27, and s. 6 of this law bore directly on its question: whether the government could negotiate or sign terms on Jerusalem.
litigation_timing.note: The law did not respond to a judgment. The Yes depends on HCJ 5167/00 having been filed before 2000-11-27, which I could not verify from a docket. The translation also says 'against this background [the resignation, effective 2000-12-12] the petitions before us were submitted', and 'were these petitions filed prior to the resignation ... we would more than likely have dismissed them'. If 5167/00 was in fact filed or refiled after 2000-11-27, the value should be No. The other joined petitions (9607/00, 84/01, 86/01, 147/01) were filed after passage.

litigation_timing.support: Searches run 2026-10-22. KNS_Bill row 170992 (ס"ח 1798, p. 432, published 2001-07-19). First-reading name 'הצעת חוק-יסוד- הכנסת (תיקון מס' 44) (הפסקת כהונה בשל עבירה שיש עמה קלון)'. The Nevo marker '(תיקון מס' 32) תשס"א-2001' sits on s. 42A, and Nevo's history note reads 'ר' סעיף 2 לענין תחולה'. The IDI page describes the Katz-Maor bill (first reading May 2001): an MK's membership would end on a court's finding of moral turpitude, without the requirement of an actual prison sentence. It names the live case as MK Yitzhak Mordechai: convicted, kalon found, suspended sentence. A WebSearch (extended) for יצחק מרדכי ערעור לבית המשפט העליון הרשעה קלון 2001 הושעה מהכנסת יחיאל לסרי returned the following. Mordechai's conviction was in the Jerusalem Magistrate's Court. His appeal was decided by the Jerusalem District Court in November 2001. His applications for leave to appeal to the Supreme Court came later (decided 2002 and 2004). He left the Knesset in March 2001. On 2001-07-09, therefore, his case was pending in the District Court, not the Supreme Court. No other Supreme Court proceeding under s. 42A or 42B was found pending then. A WebSearch (extended) for חוק-יסוד: הכנסת תיקון מס' 32 התשס"א-2001 הפסקת כהונה בשל עבירה שיש עמה קלון סעיף 42א(ב) יצחק מרדכי found nothing further.
litigation_timing.note: The law followed the Mordechai conviction, which was a trial-court judgment, not a Supreme Court judgment. The sources disagree on his status: IDI says he was suspended and replaced by Yechiel Lasri; Hebrew Wikipedia (via search summary) says he resigned, with membership ending 2001-03-28. Neither version affects the value.

litigation_timing.support: Searches run 2026-10-22. KNS_Bill row 171252 (ס"ח 1809, p. 2, published 2001-10-30). It shares the page with Basic Law: The Knesset (Amendment No. 34), BillID 171253. First-reading name 'הצעת חוק-יסוד- נשיא המדינה (תיקון מס' 6)'. Wikisource tags 'תשס"ב' on s. 11 (the President performs the functions assigned by Basic Law: The Government) and s. 12 (countersignature not required for documents on forming the government or dissolving the Knesset). No pending Supreme Court case on the President's functions or countersignature was found. No dedicated court search was possible; the judiciary database was unreachable.
litigation_timing.note: No judgment found that the law responded to. Wikisource marks this 2001 law, titled Amendment No. 6, as properly No. 5 ('[צ"ל: 5]'). A different 2003 law is also titled Amendment No. 6.

deviations: No gazette text was read for any row. fs.knesset.gov.il (and knesset.gov.il) redirect to a geo-block page (303 to maintenance-page-geo) for both WebFetch and curl. web.archive.org was refused: WebFetch reported 'unable to fetch', and curl got connection refused on port 443. Each law's subject therefore rests on: bill names in the Knesset database mirror on Hugging Face (ZeAlenu/knesset-data, KNS_Bill and KNS_BillName); Wikisource's current text and section tags; margin markers in the Nevo consolidated PDF of Basic Law: The Knesset hosted by Adalah, whose digits are partly garbled by the PDF's font encoding; and, for seq 54, 61 and 82, the WebSearch tool's own summary of the indexed gazette PDFs, which is a secondary model's reading. A reviewer should check the subjects against the gazette PDFs.

The judiciary's database was unreachable: curl to supremedecisions.court.gov.il returned an empty body, WebFetch failed with ECONNRESET, and elyon1.court.gov.il returned HTML instead of the PDF. Nevo's case search was not used (login). No filing dates were taken from a docket, and no docket-level search for pending cases was possible for any row. The No values for 57, 61, 67, 73, 79, 82, 85 and 89 rest on web and press searches finding no pending case. That is absence of evidence, not a docket check.

Seq 64 (Yes) is the row most in need of checking. It depends on HCJ 5167/00 (Weiss v. Prime Minister) having been filed before 2000-11-27, which I inferred from its docket number (about July 2000). The Versa translation's statements that the petitions were submitted against the background of the Prime Minister's resignation (effective 2000-12-12) point the other way. Only the English translation was read, not the Hebrew original. Is 'petitioners relied on the amendment and the Attorney General treated its majority requirement as limiting the outgoing government' enough for 'bearing on the subject'? That is an interpretive call and should be adjudicated.

Seq 61: Wikisource tags 'תש"ס' (the year's first law, i.e. Amendment 25) on ss. 42A and 42B, not on s. 33, and the Nevo PDF shows only Amendment 29 on s. 33. The bill name in the Knesset database ('כינוס הכנסת שלא בתקופת הכנסים') and the search tool's reading of the gazette PDF both put Amendment 25 on s. 33, and I followed them. The discrepancy is unresolved.

Seq 79: ס"ח 1898 p. 524 carries two laws, Amendment No. 6 of 2003 (temporary cessation, s. 22) and Amendment No. 7 (single candidate, s. 8). I coded Amendment No. 7 only, per the sheet's title. Two different laws are titled Amendment No. 6 to Basic Law: The President (2001 and 2003).

Seq 82: the search index lists fs.knesset.gov.il/17/law/17_lsr_300039.pdf under the title of Amendment No. 37, while the sheet and Wikisource cite 17_lsr_300158.pdf. Not resolved; the value does not depend on it.

Seq 70: IDI (page dated 2001-04-16, though it describes May 2001 events) says Mordechai was suspended and replaced by Yechiel Lasri. Wikipedia, per the search summary, says he resigned (membership ended 2001-03-28). The value does not depend on which is right.
Seq 85: one search (terms in its support field) returned material on later petitions against the enactment itself. I disregarded it and recorded no outcome.
